title: A nonzero polynomial over an algebraically closed field is a nonzero constant times a product of linear factors
statement:
Let $L$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $T$ an indeterminate and $Q\in L[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] a nonzero polynomial. Then there exist an integer $n\geq0$ and elements $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n\in L$ such that

$$
Q(T)=c\prod_{j=1}^{n}(T-\gamma_j)\quad\text{in }L[T],
$$

where $c\in L^\times$ is the leading coefficient of $Q$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient].

source.place: hidden in 'Over an algebraic closure one has $P(T)=\prod_j(1-\alpha_jT)$' (no proof given); standard: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1 (not in literature/, wanted)
